issue.title: provider: another process's provider removal is routed past for up to heldFor while requests overlap
issue.body:
`stampNowFiles` (internal/provider/hold.go) says "Another process's write is seen by the next request, as Hold's look sees it". That holds only while requests don't overlap. `Hold` stats providers.json and settings.json (`heldFreshLocked(true)`) only when `held.holds` goes from 0 to 1. While one request holds the catalog for the whole time (a long stream), a provider another process removes is still routed to by the next requests. They see it gone only once `heldFor` (1s) runs out and filememo looks at the file again.

Found while looking into jockyer's report on X (a removed provider still asked after switching models). A probe at origin/main 6f5d48ea0 did this: one goroutine holds `provider.Hold()`, providers.json is rewritten without provider `a` the way another magpie process would write it, and then a chat request for `m` (served by a and b) is sent. That request and the one right after it both went to `a`. A request sent 2.5s later went to `b`. With no hold, the first request after the write went to `b`. This bounds the gap at about a second, so it does not explain "until a restart". It does contradict the comment.

The fix could be one of:
- re-stat the two root files in `heldOf` once `heldFor` has passed since the last look, not only on a 0→1 hold;
- or reword the comment to the real bound.

comments.body:
A fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5541-overlapping-held-catalog-refresh), commit [333d97b4a](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/333d97b4ab9633c28527a7ad433f06a42d76fb49), based on `ed0ab567`.

While requests overlap, a new `Hold` now rechecks the providers and settings roots once per `heldFor` window. A changed root invalidates held values and stale in-flight publication; waiting callers check the generation before using a shared build. Values already returned to an active request remain unchanged, and unchanged roots keep the cached path.

A deterministic regression uses real external file writes and reproduces the stale removal on the base. Virtual time and barriers check the expiry boundary, within-window reuse, restore, in-flight builders, waiting callers and timeout; removing generation invalidation makes the regression fail. Parent related provider tests passed under `-race`; provider vet and the full offline `nogui` build passed before the final test-only addition.

The two root files are not an atomic filesystem snapshot; concurrent environment changes during a hold, other platforms and the full suite were not tested. AI-assisted implementation and review.
